title: AI's Market Path Will Get Bumpier
gist: Mohamed A. El-Erian frames the US economy and markets as caught in a 'generational race' between AI's enormous potential to raise productivity and earnings by enhancing intelligence as an input, and the unintended consequences of the technology that could slow the pace and depth of its adoption; this is a paywalled teaser excerpt.

themes.theme: AI's growth promise versus adoption risk

insights.claim: El-Erian frames the US economy and financial markets as being in a 'generational race' between AI and related technologies' massive potential to unlock productivity and earnings growth on one hand, and the unintended consequences of these technologies on the other, with implications extending well beyond future prosperity to financial stability.
insights.speaker: Mohamed A. El-Erian
insights.so_what: Positions AI's economic impact as a two-sided race rather than a one-directional productivity boom -- a framework for weighing AI-driven earnings upside against systemic/financial-stability downside risk in portfolio construction.
insights.quote: The race is between AI and related technologies that hold massive potential to unlock productivity and earnings growth, on the one hand, and the unintended consequences of these technologies, on the other.
insights.locator: MILAN—The US economy and its financial markets

insights.claim: AI's potential to drive higher economic growth is enormous because it enhances intelligence, an input that goes into nearly everything the economy does.
insights.speaker: Mohamed A. El-Erian
insights.so_what: Frames AI's economic impact via a general-purpose-technology lens (intelligence as a universal input) rather than a narrow sector story, supporting a broad-based rather than sector-specific view of AI's growth contribution.
insights.quote: By enhancing the input that goes into so much of what we do—intelligence—AI's potential to drive higher economic growth is enormous.

insights.claim: Fears about AI's unintended consequences are affecting the pace and depth of the technology's adoption, meaning the promise of long-term gains must be weighed against more immediate risks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed A. El-Erian
insights.so_what: Flags adoption-pace risk (driven by public/institutional fear of unintended consequences) as a distinct variable from AI capability risk -- worth tracking sentiment/adoption surveys as a leading indicator for whether AI capex assumptions need repricing.
insights.locator: with fears of the technology's unintended consequences affecting the pace and depth of adoption
